headline: Chicago Woman Creates Monarch Butterfly Sanctuaries Across City
meta_description: A Chicago resident transformed her home into a native plant sanctuary for migrating monarchs, sparking eight similar projects at homes and schools.
summary_short: One Chicago woman's passion for monarch butterflies led her to create native plant habitats—first at her own home, then at eight additional locations across the city.
body:
A Chicago woman turned her home into a sanctuary for monarch butterflies undertaking their nearly 3,000-mile migration to Mexico. What began as a personal project has blossomed into something far larger.

Inspired by the monarch's remarkable journey, she has since created eight native plant projects at homes and schools throughout the area. Each space provides vital resources—native plants that serve as food and shelter—for the delicate butterflies as they travel between continents.

Her work demonstrates how individual action can scale into community impact. By establishing multiple sanctuaries rather than stopping at one, she has multiplied the help available to these vulnerable pollinators during their critical migration season.
quick_facts: Chicago woman created monarch butterfly sanctuary in her home
Monarchs migrate nearly 3,000 miles to Mexico annually
Project expanded to eight native plant sites at homes and schools
